findings.summary: Cancelled-with-zero-jobs fingerprint: ~24m37s between created_at and updated_at yet Jobs API reports zero jobs for attempt 1, artifacts zero, and the fetched raw log is a 0-byte body with HTTP-success status. For this workflow configuration the ONLY state consistent with all of these plus the concurrency group is queued-the-whole-time-then-cancelled (a run executing or having executed jobs would retain job records even when cancelled mid-flight). The emptiness could in principle also be a bundle-side fetch failure rather than ground truth; local sources cannot distinguish the two, so live-API adjudication should precede any prune decision.

Root-cause mechanism identified in DURABLE Git config (not in any log): the Product Supervisor cancels exactly this situation by design. product-supervisor.yml:53-62 reads: 'Direct workflow_run triggers can enqueue a stale Product decision while a long beta is already executing. If a real Product run is in_progress, queued Product-main runs are redundant' — then executes `gh run cancel "$queued_id"` for every queued/pending product-loop run. The precondition (another product-loop main run in_progress throughout 20:22:45Z-20:47:22Z) is proven by sibling run 32886859788's architect commit at 20:31:13Z and builder commit at 20:58:59Z. Supervisor cron fires at :19/:49 hourly; GitHub schedule delivery jitter makes the 20:47:22Z cancel time cadence-consistent, but the SPECIFIC cancelling supervisor instance is NOT attributable from available sources (its logs are not in the bundle and supervisor runs themselves are hygiene-prunable). What IS established: mechanism class exists and fits; which instance fired remains unknown.

Positive economics observation: the dedupe layer worked as intended at near-zero cost. A workflow_run trigger (some Graph/Physics/Intel/Runtime lane completion per product-loop.yml trigger config; specific upstream run not identifiable) enqueued a redundant Product decision WHILE the PB-001 v4 architect->builder chain was executing; the queued duplicate was cancelled before consuming any runner minute or agent token (no job ever started). Without it, a second director session would have raced the executing lineage on lab/product. This is the first distilled instance of the supervisor's queued-run dedupe actually firing.

Cancelled-while-queued runs are forensically invisible: no jobs, no logs, no artifacts, no receipt naming the canceller. Reconstructing this event required cross-referencing sibling cycle branches' commit timestamps against the window and reading supervisor source. The supervisor's own evidence (::warning:: 'Cancelling stale queued Product run <id>') lives only in SUPERVISOR run logs, which are themselves routinely deleted by repo hygiene (2 Product Supervisor deletions already occurred in the 102-run incident). Extends CF-2026-08-25-02 (receipt gap): queue-state transitions and cancellations need run-id-attributed durable receipts too, or every future occurrence costs the same archaeology.

Coverage-gap note (metadata/Git-derived, NOT a loss claim): run_number 9 implies six intervening product-loop invocations (#3-#8) between distilled records #1 (32799261473) and #2 (32820217763). Five intervening Git lineages exist without runs/ records: cycle/product/{32851946087/architect, 32861115761/{architect,builder}, 32870361258/{architect,builder}, 32886859788/{architect,builder}} plus persistent branch pb001-architect-v3, and lab/product carries additional director-session commits citing 32851946087 and 32870361258. None of these ids appears in EITHER deletion manifest (102-run hygiene set or the earlier 21-run one-shot set), so their raw Actions logs were not pruned by known events and may still be server-retrievable. id-to-run-number mapping unverified.
